matches.quote: Field dependence of the drop, I-V characteristics, critical current and a Meissner signal are not shown; Ref. [20] is cited instead.
The authors should give a table with thickness, geometry, growth method, contact configuration, excitation current and extracted temperatures for every sample
The c-axis value of 12.278 Å attributed to "nanoscale single crystals" appears to come from powder XRD (Rigaku Miniflex) on the parent material, not on the measured flakes.
The statements that impurity-induced disorder "cannot explain this phenomenon", that "the distortion in RuO6 octahedra is eliminated" (abstract, pp. 4 and 6)... are therefore assertions, not results.
The supporting diamagnetism (p. 5) is neither shown nor quantified for these samples... the diamagnetism discussion should be softened or backed by nanoflake magnetization data
sample 4 (10 nm) and sample 5 (30 nm) are superconducting/Bose glass, while samples 1 and 2 (25 nm) and sample 3 (35 nm) are Mott insulators
Thickness does not order the phases... sample 4 (10 nm) and sample 5 (30 nm) are superconducting/Bose glass, while samples 1 and 2 (25 nm)... are Mott insulators
Samples 6 and 7 on LaAlO3 (50 nm) have a shorter c axis... stronger RuO6 distortion. Yet they show Bose-glass behaviour... while the supposedly less distorted 25-35 nm flakes 1-3 are Mott insulators.
The temperature windows are too narrow to tell ρ ~ ln(1/T) from σ ~ ln T... about 210-299 K (a factor of about 1.35) for samples 1-3 (Fig. 2b).
A phase entered at 220 K and left at about 100 K on cooling is a finite-temperature crossover, not a ground state, yet the boundaries are called quantum critical points
The scaling L² = D T^(−p) with p = 1 fixed (p. 7) is not justified at these temperatures.
In the Fisher framework the Bose glass is an insulating, compressible T = 0 phase with zero conductivity... a finite-conductivity bosonic state is usually called a Bose or anomalous metal.

C9 notes Tc(10 nm) < Tc(30 nm), which is subsumed under P5's critique that thickness does not monotonically order the phases across the 10-35 nm samples ('partly').
